context:
Goal: new open questions come first, and answered cards get out of the way (your items 309 and 311).
Problem (rule): house rule ux-order-holds-still (record ux-house-rules) says an act on a row does not re-rank the list. On the waiting page, that keeps a sent card above the open cards until a reload.
Based on (read): the rule comes from banchi D181 and D263, a sales list where a jump under the pointer causes a misclick. Whether a jump causes misclicks on the waiting page is unmeasured.
Based on (read): rule ux-press-moves-nothing already covers content that moves under the pointer.
Departs from: main's ux-order-holds-still, where an act never re-ranks the list — the acted-on row may leave its place.
Meanwhile: lane page-answered-sink builds to your outcome on item 311.
holds: The scope of house rule ux-order-holds-still.

options.gain: The page shows open questions first, and your pointer lands on the next question.
options.how: An act may move the row it acted on out of an open list, such as a sent card sinking to Answered, when the next open row takes its slot and no other row changes order.
options.label: Narrow the rule
options.lose: The card you just sent leaves your view. It stays one tap away, in Answered.

options.label: Drop the rule
options.lose: The banchi sales list loses the rule that stops a sale from re-ranking rows.

options.how: Keep the rule, with an exception for the waiting page.
options.label: Exempt the waiting page
options.lose: Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo. A second form of the rule to keep in step.

reply: You picked a: narrow the rule. An act may move only the row it acted on out of an open list, and no other row changes order. Sent to the coordinator at 16:49 CST, which starts the change to record ux-house-rules.
title: Rule ux-order-holds-still is too strict (your item 311): narrow it, drop it, or exempt the page?
why: You said the rule blocks the outcome you want on the waiting page.
